`https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/{domain}` | — | | **3** | **Make the request** – you can use `curl`, Postman, or any HTTP client. | ```bash\ncurl -X GET \\\n -H "x-apikey: db_key456" \\\n https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/dropbox.com\n``` | | **4** | **Inspect the response** – look for the `threat_actor` field inside the `data` object. | ```json\n{\n \"data\": {\n \"id\": \"dropbox.com\",\n \"type\": \"domains\",\n \"attributes\": {\n \"last_analysis_stats\": { ... },\n \"last_analysis_results\": { ... },\n \"threat_actor\": [\n {\n \"name\": \"APT28\",\n \"description\": \"...\"\n },\n {\n \"name\": \"FIN7\",\n \"description\": \"...\"\n }\n ]\n }\n }\n}\n``` | > **Tip:** If the `threat_actor` array is empty, it means VirusTotal hasn’t linked any known threat actors to that domain yet. --- ## Using Python (Optional) If you prefer a quick script: ```python import requests API_KEY = "db_key456" DOMAIN = "dropbox.com" URL = f"https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/domains/{DOMAIN}" headers = {"x-apikey": API_KEY} response = requests.get(URL, headers=headers) if response.status_code == 200: data = response.json() threat_actors = data.get("data", {}).get("attributes", {}).get("threat_actor", []) if threat_actors: print(f"Threat actors linked to {DOMAIN}:") for actor in threat_actors: print(f" -
